note: Lookbacks are declared in BARS, never calendar days, so the normalisation window a z-score names is exact. Pairs sharing a ratioFamilyId collapse to one evidence family before any confirmation arithmetic.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means gold outperforming silver, historically a defensive rotation within precious metals.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: Both legs are ETF proxies for spot metal, not the metal itself; ETF expense and roll differ from spot.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means semiconductors outperforming the broad market, conventionally read as risk-on.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: Index-tracking ETF proxy; constituent weights differ between semiconductor indices.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means semiconductors outperforming the broad market, conventionally read as risk-on.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: Overlaps SOXX/SPY heavily by construction; the shared ratioFamilyId is what stops the two counting as independent confirmation.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means high-yield credit outperforming intermediate Treasuries, conventionally read as spread compression.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: An ETF-price proxy for credit spreads, not an option-adjusted spread; duration differs between legs.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means small caps outperforming large caps, conventionally read as broadening participation.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: Size-factor proxy; sector composition differs materially between the two indices.

pairs.directionConvention: Rising means developed international equities outperforming US equities.
pairs.provenanceCaveat: Legs settle on different market sessions and carry unhedged currency exposure; this pair must clear session and FX alignment before it emits a reading.
